newsitem.title: USA: Chicago City Council approves TIF bonds and plans.
newsitem.headline: Chicago City Council approves TIF bonds and plans.

text.p: Chicago City Council on Wednesday approved tax increment financing plans for the downtown theater district, residential housing redevelopment and a riverwalk connecting the Loop with the Chinatown neighborhood.
City Council approved issuing $195 million of bonds for various projects in the theater district, including development of new facilities and the reconstruction of an elevated train station.
The council also approved creating a TIF district for an area north of downtown that includes the Cabrini-Green public housing complex to finance a $281 million redevelopment plan.

The near north district includes about 340 acres encompassing one of the oldest neighborhoods in the city. Plans for the area include housing for lower, middle and upper income residents and envision new police, fire and library facilities.

The near south side of Chicago also received a tax increment financing district with the designation of an area along the Chicago River for a walkway to connect the Loop with the nearby Chinatown neighborhood.
The $14 million walkway would run 1.25 miles and could take up to five years to develop.
